## Shipping this repo with sklp

These spaces are **reconciled by core from the default branch**. A merge to main reaches the node within seconds. **Never `sklp deploy apply` them**: it pushes your local file to whatever context is active and is undone by the next reconcile.

| Space | Manifest | Node |
|---|---|---|
| `vvaves-production` | `.sklp/vvaves/deploy.yaml` | `sklet-prod-v2` |

**Image watches**: publishing a new tag of these images rolls the service by itself (no apply, no manifest edit):

| Image | Service | Space |
|---|---|---|
| `rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/vvaves/core` | `app` | `vvaves-production` |
| `rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/vvaves/migrate` | `migrate` | `vvaves-production` |
| `rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/vvaves/tts` | `tts` | `vvaves-production` |
| `rg.fr-par.scw.cloud/vvaves/web` | `web` | `vvaves-production` |

**Pipelines** (`sklp run <name>`): `ci`, `generate`, `publish`

### How a change ships

1. `sklp flow start <name>` → work → `sklp flow end` (opens the PR).
2. Merge the PR. A manifest change (`.sklp/**/deploy.yaml`) is live once core reconciles main.
3. Image change: from a clean main, `sklp run publish…`; the watch rolls it.

### When a change does not land

Core rejects a whole manifest that references a secret the project lacks (or one not deploy-readable), and then applies nothing from it. Check names with `sklp secret list -project <id>` (`sklp whoami -json` gives the id). `sklp deploy restart` only restarts what the node already holds; it never reads git.

Read the live state with `-json`: `sklp whoami -json`, `sklp deploy ls -json`, `sklp deploy mesh ls -json`, `sklp deploy datastores -json`, `sklp deploy restores -json`.
